EDIT `polygon-form4-fetcher_test.ts` (+6 tests: single-page grouping, next_url pagination, 403/404, missing-tickers drop, multi-ticker tickers[0] attribution). EDIT `insider-orchestrator.ts` (Step 2 restructure — market-wide fetch → filter qualifying tickers → per-qualifying-ticker shares+price+compute; market-wide entitlement gate translates to per-ticker typed skips; market-wide throw → per-ticker `fetch_error` skips). EDIT `insider-orchestrator_test.ts` (mock `fetchForm4MarketWide` returning a Map; all 12 existing scenarios preserved byte-identical assertions). EDIT `docs/04-modules/longshort/signals/insider-transactions.md` (Architecture section + a new "FP-042 / ACT-155 market-wide-fetch addendum" subsection). EDIT `docs/07-reference/function-index.md` (PolygonForm4Fetcher entry updated for the new public method). NO new migration / permission / route / env-var / npm dep. |
| **Evidence** | (a) Gate 11 (Deno) scoped to FP-042 changed files — **76 passed / 0 failed** across `polygon-form4-fetcher_test.ts` (16 — was 10, +6 market-wide), `compute-insider_test.ts` (26 — unchanged, byte-identical), `insider-orchestrator_test.ts` (12 — assertions preserved), `longshort-insider-compute/index_test.ts` (7), `longshort-insider-compute-manual/index_test.ts` (9), `polygon-shares-outstanding-fetcher_test.ts` (untouched, 10), other reused shared infra. (b) Gate 4 ESLint scoped to the 4 changed files (`polygon-form4-fetcher.ts`, `polygon-form4-fetcher_test.ts`, `insider-orchestrator.ts`, `insider-orchestrator_test.ts`) — **0 errors / 0 warnings**. (c) Anti-pattern guards: typed-absence preserved (`subscription_gated` / `data_unavailable` / `missing_shares_outstanding` / `no_qualifying_transactions` / `fetch_error`); divide-by-zero guard on `market_cap` preserved at the orchestrator chokepoint; no `Date.now()` / wall-clock — the gte/lte window derives from `as_of`; no `any`; no `eslint-disable`. (d) Same-PR Rule 6 — code + signals doc + function-index updated together. |
| **CPU math** | Before: 839 Form 4 + 839 shares + 839 price = 2517 HTTPS + 839 JSON parses + 839 regex/decay loops. After: ~1–5 Form 4 (paginated, larger pages) + N shares + N price where N = qualifying tickers (typically <100 in a 90-day window) + N compute loops. Net: ~2300 fewer HTTPS round-trips + ~840 fewer JSON parses + ~750 fewer compute loops per run. Well under the ~2 s cumulative-CPU isolate budget. |

### ACT-298 — insider-discovery post-write verification: PK-triple predicate (2026-06-18 red, Hypothesis A reconciled)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Date** | 2026-06-23 |
| **Mode** | EXECUTION (Tier A; verification-predicate fix only — write path unchanged) |
| **HEAD (pre)** | `a6e68260` |
| **Authority** | Supervisor; live-DB reconciliation (Claude + Lovable) of the 2026-06-23 GHA `insider-discovery` daily fire (correlation_id `dc50848f-2c54-4096-a38a-bb1d0f80e132`, `discovered_by=gha-daily`, `as_of=2026-06-18`) which exited 2 with `insider_discovery_supabase_failure: post-write verification found zero rows for discovery_correlation_id=dc50848f…` despite a 201 insert of 180 rows. Decisive ground-truth query: `SELECT as_of_date, discovery_correlation_id, count(*) FROM insider_accession_discovery_queue WHERE as_of_date='2026-06-18' GROUP BY …` → one row, **n=180**, correlation_id **`723b5f5d-744b-47bb-bf84-059bbab5b4cd`** (the 2026-06-20 run), discovered_at 2026-06-20 09:33:25 UTC; rows under `dc50848f…` = **0**. Confirms HYPOTHESIS A: benign idempotent re-run + verification-predicate bug. The 180 PK-triples all collided with the prior run's rows; `Prefer: resolution=ignore-duplicates,return=minimal` correctly suppressed every insert (201 with empty body — PostgREST gives no inserted-count signal under `return=minimal`). The old `verifyPersistedCount(env, thisRunCorrelationId)` predicate threw on zero because `ignore-duplicates` legitimately drops the new label on PKs that already exist — even though every accession this run discovered IS in the table, under the prior run's id. HYPOTHESIS B (real write hole) excluded by the live-DB query. |
| **Scope** | Verification-predicate replacement + log-key relabel + idempotent-re-run telemetry. EDITED 3 files: `scripts/insider-discovery-egress.ts` (added `verifyPersistedPkTriples` + `PkTriple`/`PkVerificationResult` exports; wrapped CLI inserter to capture submitted PK-triples; replaced the failure predicate from `persistedByCorrelation === 0` to `pkVerification.missing.length > 0`; renamed `rows_inserted → rows_submitted` in the run-complete log; added `submitted_pk_triples`/`present_after_verify`/`missing_after_verify`/`idempotent_rerun` log fields; positive `insider_discovery_idempotent_rerun` event emit on the benign-re-run path); `scripts/insider-discovery-egress_test.ts` (3 new hermetic tests `(c5a/b/c)`); this entry. NO write-path change (the `makeRestInserter` POST + `resolution=ignore-duplicates,return=minimal` is byte-unchanged). NO migration. NO schema change. NO cron arming. |
| **The fix — precise (not cheap) form** | `verifyPersistedPkTriples` asserts presence of every submitted `(as_of_date, issuer_cik, accession_number)` triple via per-day readback (`?select=issuer_cik,accession_number&as_of_date=eq.<day>` paged at 1000/page) intersected set-wise with the submitted day-bucket. SUCCESS iff every submitted triple is present **regardless of which `discovery_correlation_id` labels it** (a prior run's id is the same row). FAILURE only when a submitted triple is genuinely **missing** after the insert (the real write-hole / Hypothesis-B case the verification SHOULD catch). The cheaper "count by `as_of_date >= expected`" form was explicitly rejected per scope: it would pass if a DIFFERENT 180 rows existed for the day while these specific accessions were missing (partial-run masking). PK-triple intersect is bounded by per-day row count (~180/day in production) so URL-length is not a concern; pagination is in place for safety. |
| **Log relabel + telemetry** | `insider_discovery_run_complete`: `rows_inserted` → `rows_submitted` (PostgREST `return=minimal` gives no server-confirmed inserted-count, so the old name was a mislabel — the proximate source of the 2026-06-18 log self-contradiction); added `submitted_pk_triples`/`present_after_verify`/`missing_after_verify`/`idempotent_rerun` (booleans + counts derived from the new verifier); retained `persisted_rows_by_correlation_id` as diagnostic (zero with `present_after_verify == submitted` is now positively flagged as `idempotent_rerun=true`). New `insider_discovery_idempotent_rerun` event emits ONLY on the benign all-duplicates path (all submitted PKs present AND zero rows under this run's id AND expectedWrites > 0) so the next operator does not have to infer the benign case from log contradictions. Internal `DayOutcome.rows_inserted` field kept unchanged to bound test blast radius; the rename is on the JSON log keys (operator-facing). |
| **Tests** | 32 baseline `deno test scripts/insider-discovery-egress_test.ts` → all 32 green pre-change; **35 post-change, 35 green** (32 baseline + 3 new): `(c5a) verifyPersistedPkTriples: all submitted PKs present (benign idempotent re-run) → 0 missing` (pins the 2026-06-18 regression — the case that used to throw now passes), `(c5b) verifyPersistedPkTriples: a submitted PK genuinely missing (real write hole) → reported in missing[]` (pins the Hypothesis-B condition the new predicate MUST still catch), `(c5c) empty submitted set short-circuits` (no readback fetch when nothing was submitted). |
| **Live data state (post-diagnosis, pre-fix)** | `insider_accession_discovery_queue` for `as_of_date='2026-06-18'` = **180 rows present + intact** under correlation_id `723b5f5d-744b-47bb-bf84-059bbab5b4cd` (the 2026-06-20 first run). Zero rows under `dc50848f…`. The data pipeline was healthy throughout; the 2026-06-23 red was purely cosmetic-CI (the verification-predicate bug). No data recovery needed; the F2.c consumer (`seedWorkItems`) drains by `(as_of_date, consumed_at IS NULL)` — correlation_id is not part of its claim predicate, so the prior-id-labelled rows are claimable as normal. |
| **Out-of-scope guarantees** | Write path byte-unchanged: `makeRestInserter` POST + `Prefer: resolution=ignore-duplicates,return=minimal` + `insider_discovery_supabase_insert` event (with `attempted_rows` which is already accurately named) all unchanged. Zero migration / schema change. Zero touch to F2.c consumer / `insider-work-list-registration.ts` / `insider-queue-bootstrap.ts`. Zero cron arming. The legacy `verifyPersistedCount` helper retained for telemetry use (no longer load-bearing for the failure decision). |
| **Catalog crossing — POSTGREST `return=minimal` GIVES NO INSERTED-COUNT** | New forward-binding class (candidate Catalog entry on next firing): when a producer uses `Prefer: resolution=ignore-duplicates,return=minimal` against PostgREST, the response body is empty and there is NO server-side signal distinguishing "inserted N" from "inserted 0, suppressed N". Post-write verification MUST therefore assert **the intended natural-key presence**, NOT a count tagged by a per-run label that idempotent re-runs legitimately drop. Producers MAY log a submitted-count (with that exact name), but MUST NOT call it an inserted-count. This firing is single — the catalog row will be opened on the second firing per the §22.8.5 two-observation rule. |
| **ROI Impact** | Zero on prediction / signal / sizing / execution (the data was already present and correctly drainable by the consumer; the bug was in the CI exit code path, not the trading data). Positive on CI gate health (eliminates the benign-re-run false-fail class) and on diagnostic clarity (the next genuine write hole will surface with a precise `missing[N of M] (cik,accession)` message instead of an ambiguous zero-correlation-id message). |
| **Status** | Closed (ACT-298, 2026-06-23). |

| **Critical safety invariant — PURE JSON READ** | The script uses `Deno.readTextFile` + `JSON.parse` exclusively. (b) `deno run --allow-read scripts/check-lockfile-versions.ts` against the live repo → `check-lockfile-versions: CLEAN — both lockfiles at version "3"` exit 0. (c) SHA-256 of `deno.lock` + `supabase/functions/deno.lock` byte-identical before vs after running the script + tests (root `59216bfd…`, functions `581b66ac…`) — the safety invariant holds empirically. (d) Self-grep confirms no `deno cache` / `Deno.run` / `Deno.Command` / `child_process` / `exec(` in code positions. |

Both resolve `eslint.config.js` via ESLint's normal flat-config discovery; no `--config`, no `--no-eslintrc`, no alternate path. (2) **Why the other four sites did NOT fail #379.** `eslint.config.js` lines 27–37 set `"@typescript-eslint/ban-ts-comment": "off"` for a glob set: `**/*_test.ts`, `scripts/**/*.ts`, `**/test-fixtures.ts`, `src/features/longshort/services/broker/**/*.ts`. The four other sites are genuinely out-of-scope of the rule and safe — no whack-a-mole. (3) **Is `@ts-expect-error` the correct standard?** Generally yes (it errors if the suppression becomes unnecessary), BUT it requires a real TS error on the next line — and `supabase/functions/**` is OUTSIDE `tsconfig.app.json`'s `include: ["src"]`, so tsc never typechecks this file in CI. The `declare const Deno: …` ambient declaration produces zero TS error in any CI gate. Per the operator STOP condition ("if the declare is error-free under CI's tsc, the directive should be DELETED, not converted"), the directive is removed. |

Resolution (reconciled): align the DEC wording to the code. The code's episode-counting is the correct and superior bound for two reasons — (i) the "rank-positions-scanned" phrasing was written under the now-obsolete assumption that the kernel made live per-rank borrow-locate calls (per-rank API cost); clause (j).4's purity discipline made pre-flight results INJECTED, so there is NO per-rank I/O cost in the pure kernel and the position-counting rationale evaporated; (ii) literal position-counting would be a behavior regression — a single slot facing a wall of sector-illegal ranks 21–30 could exhaust the entire side budget and starve other failing slots, whereas episode-counting distributes the budget across failing slots. This is a wording-only amendment to clause (j).2 / (j).3 + the named-constants table footnote + an audit-facing worst-case-envelope addition. **NO code change, NO test change, NO migration, NO behavior change** — the code is correct; the DEC text is being aligned to it. |

### ACT-457-ADD-03 — W2.4 R-1 qualification-semantics adjustment + `overshoot-study-run` edge fn (2026-07-03)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Head** | `66d5839e` → in-turn edits. |
| **Scope** | R-1 (qualification vs argmax) reconciled AGREE; ONE migration adding `excess_w1..excess_w5` NULL numeric columns to the empty `overshoot_study_candidate_events`; `event-detection.sql` + `cell-aggregation.sql` + `event-detection_fixture_test.sql` updated; NEW `supabase/functions/overshoot-study-run/index.ts`; docs. |
| **R-1 Lovable position (formed independently)** | AGREE with qualification. The study's primary deliverable is a per-configuration arrival-rate grid. A live detector configured `(W, band)` fires whenever `\|excess_W\| ≥ band`, regardless of whether some other window would have shown a larger excess. ARGMAX partitioning arbitrarily suppresses same-event participation in shorter/longer cells and would systematically understate arrival rates in cells that share their band-crossings with a "louder" neighbor cell. Per-cell independence is the design intent — cross-cell double-counting is a feature, not a leak. |
| **R-1 supervisor position (verbatim)** | "The grid's W dimension must use QUALIFICATION semantics (cell (W,band) counts events whose W-day \|excess\| crosses the band, since that is what a live detector configured (W,band) fires on; argmax partitioning understates per-config arrival rates, the primary deliverable)." |
| **R-1 resolution** | AGREE, implemented in-turn. Event persisted once per `(ticker, event_date, side)`; qualification predicate is `EXISTS W: \|excess_W\| ≥ min_band_bps`; ALL FIVE per-window excesses (`excess_w1..w5`) persisted on the event row; argmax `move_pct` + `window_days` retained as descriptive columns; cell aggregation derives membership by `\|excess_wN\| ≥ band` per-cell. |
| **W2.3 attestation corrections** | Two corrections to ACT-457-ADD-02 self-attestation. (1) Guard-workflow CI was mischaracterized as "N/A this turn" — `overshoot-guards.yml`'s push trigger is unconditional and `_shared/overshoot/study/**` is inside the guarded glob, so the W2.3 push DID run the workflow (v2.9.1 pin held; result GREEN — no failure entries on the run). ## ACT-457-ADD-06 — FP-069 W2.5 D-2 postgres.js unknown-type param class fix (2026-07-04)

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| **Mode** | EXECUTION (W2.5 D-2 conditional scope-expansion, operator-AUTHORIZED after Option 1 → §9 escalate-to-class ruling). |
| **HEAD** | `9250bb30` at fix time; W2.5 closure landed at `64df16db`. |
| **Framing (honest)** | Bug is **latent from W2.4**, **uncovered by W2.5** — NOT caused by W2.5. The `CASE ... / 10000.0` in `cell-aggregation.sql.ts` §B has always required `::numeric` casting under postgres.js `unsafe(sql, params)`, but the dry-run path introduced in W2.4 skips `CELL_AGGREGATION_SQL` entirely, so the `text / numeric` operator-resolution error remained untriggered until D-2b (first-ever live end-to-end). Two D-2 live probe failures (`corr:6e278b3e`, `corr:fb4ee9ee`) — the first surfaced by a `console.error` addition in the catch block, the second read from edge-function logs. |
| **Root cause** | postgres.js binds JS scalars as unknown/text-typed positional params. Any `:name` used in an arithmetic / date-compare / uuid-compare context must carry an adjacent `::type` cast, or postgres resolves the surrounding operator against text and raises `42883 operator does not exist: text / numeric` (or the date equivalent). |
| **C1 — cast fix (byte-identical semantics)** | 6 `::date` casts added in `event-detection.sql.ts` (bars_snapshot_max_date, earnings_snapshot_max_date, lookback_min_date, event_date_min in WHERE clauses; `ec.announcement_date::date` in earnings sub-selects). 2 `::numeric` casts in `cell-aggregation.sql.ts` §B (`:haircut_bps_long::numeric`, `:haircut_bps_short::numeric`). 3 pre-existing casts preserved (`:min_band_bps::numeric`, existing uuid casts). `bindNamed` uses `:name\b` — word-boundary regex preserves adjacent `::type`. |
| **Post-fix probes** | D-2a BOOT (dry, 90d): 200 / 47.7s / 39,857 events (run `8ebcde1c…c07c`, corr `308d6ef6…9fa1`). D-2b LIVE (dry_run:false, 90d): **200 / 58.9s / 39,857 events / 6,000 cells** (run `045d2dfc…2700`, corr `a4210029…422f`) — **first-ever successful live end-to-end**. DB rows: D-2a `outcome='partial'` + `DRY_RUN:` prefix (accepted convention); D-2b `outcome='completed'`. Three boot-probe vindications total (D-1, D-2a-pre-fix, D-2a-post-fix all 2xx). |

| **T6 — Live-config arrival preview (from `overshoot_study_candidate_events`, upper-bound — exclusion NOT applied)** | SQL: three configs computed via `WITH windows/cfg/trading_days AS (…) SELECT cfg.label, side, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ABS(move_pct)>=cfg.min_move AND window_days<=cfg.max_w AND event_date BETWEEN full_min AND full_max) AS events_full, … / (SELECT td_full FROM trading_days) AS ev_per_td_full, …` for `[2022-03-08, 2026-07-02]` (full: 1,084 trading days) and `[2025-07-02, 2026-07-02]` (l12m: 252 trading days). Verbatim: **C1 |m|≥7% w≤2 excl5:** `long: 5,713 events_full, 5.270/td_full, 1,970 events_l12m, 7.817/td_l12m`; `short: 4,629 events_full, 4.270/td_full, 1,491 events_l12m, 5.917/td_l12m`. **C2 |m|≥10% w≤3 excl5:** `long: 5,075 / 4.682/td / 1,745 / 6.925/td`; `short: 4,006 / 3.696/td / 1,236 / 4.905/td`. **C3 |m|≥15% w≤5 excl5:** `long: 8,026 / 7.404/td / 2,825 / 11.210/td`; `short: 5,434 / 5.013/td / 1,644 / 6.524/td`. **W3 capacity-realism against 20 slots/side (upper bound before exclusion; T3 shows exclusion at width=5 shrinks arrivals ~26%):** every plausible config produces 4–11 candidate arrivals per trading day per side — MULTIPLES of the 20-slot capacity per DAY. Capacity is not the binding constraint; the entry-quality gate (band + momentum + drawdown + exclusion) is. This is the W3 headline: the strategy is arrival-rich, and W3's live detector will need to prioritize among competing simultaneous candidates on ranking (mq × db × band × turnover-tolerance) rather than accept-all. Exclusion (width 5) reduces these numbers by ~26% per T3 — call C2 with excl=5 an effective ~3.5 long + ~2.7 short per trading day, still >10× the daily-fill capacity for a 20-slot book at typical half-day turnover. Note: C3 (widest window `w≤5`) has HIGHER event counts than C2 (narrower `w≤3`) because widening the window admits slower dislocations, even at the higher move threshold — the `window ≤ W` semantic captures all argmax-window ≤ W, so widening W is additive on arrivals. |

| **Objective evidence** | `git diff ef8c5730~1 ef8c5730 --stat -- supabase/functions/deno.lock deno.lock` → ` supabase/functions/deno.lock \| 156 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++` (+156 additions, 0 deletions). Root `deno.lock` = untouched. ACT-461.b's report stated "`deno.lock` untouched" without qualifying which of the two files nor citing a diff — a categorical assertion that omitted the load-bearing +156 change. |
| **Mechanism of the miss (reconciliation (a))** | The check inspected byte-sizes reported by `ls -la` on `bun.lockb` and `package-lock.json` (both truly untouched) and mentally generalized the assertion to `deno.lock` without ever running a `git diff` on the two Deno lockfiles. The +156-line growth is legitimate and expected — `basis-fidelity_test.ts` imports `postgres` (postgresjs) which pulls the `std@0.132.0` crypto subtree into `supabase/functions/deno.lock`; this closure is load-bearing for `deno test --lock=supabase/functions/deno.lock` runs of the harness in CI. But the CHARACTERIZATION in the report was wrong: "untouched" is factually false for that file. |
| **Additive correction (b)** | ACT-461.b's Gates row is superseded on the lockfile line only. Correct statement: `git diff ef8c5730~1 ef8c5730 --stat -- supabase/functions/deno.lock deno.lock` → `supabase/functions/deno.lock \| 156 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++` (root untouched; functions lock gained +156 for the postgresjs → std@0.132.0 crypto transitive closure — legitimate, load-bearing for `--lock` harness runs). All other ACT-461.b evidence (parity ALL-MATCH, gate results, scope compliance) stands unchanged. |
| **Rule upgrade (c) — machine-checkable form binding forward** | Every report's lockfile line MUST be the pasted output of `git diff <pre-turn-SHA> HEAD --stat -- supabase/functions/deno.lock deno.lock`. An assertion without the paste IS drift (regardless of whether the underlying claim is true). Empty diff → paste-with-note (`(no diff — HEAD == <pre-turn-SHA>)`). Non-empty diff → paste verbatim + one-line legitimacy rationale (which dependency closure, why load-bearing). This makes the rule executable at review time — an ACT entry missing the paste fails on inspection without needing to re-derive anything. |

## PEAD SHELVE — closure filings (2026-07-14, operator-accepted)

**(1) Mechanism note (why the shelve is structural, not sample-dependent).**
PEAD's measured alpha is concentrated in the announcement gap — the price move between the T+0 announcement (BMO/AMC) and the T+1 open. Once entry basis is moved to T+1-open (the only implementable entry for a scheduled-event strategy without pre-market execution machinery), the harvestable residual collapses 71–95 % vs the T+0-close v1 numbers. This is a **structural mechanism finding**, not a small-sample noise result: the gap is unharvestable at T+1-open under any winsorization / cell-slicing we can apply. Corpus expansion (ACT-522 backfill) or L/S long-only sleeving will not close the gap because the gap is the alpha. **PEAD does not re-open unless (a) pre-market execution lands as its own charter, or (b) a different mechanism than post-announcement drift is proposed.** Filed alongside `artifacts/ACT-521-RESULTS-pead-honesty-gates-rerun.md`.

**(2) ACT-522 downgrade → data-hygiene backlog.**
**Priority: LOW (data-hygiene, batch-when-convenient).** Code fix already merged in `earnings-calendar-fetcher.ts` (field names `epsActual`/`revenueActual`/`epsEstimated`/`revenueEstimated`); DB backfill of the 355,184 FMP-source rows deferred indefinitely. Rationale: repairs the corpus and enables future re-tests, but is NOT strategy work and consumes no urgency budget. Will be batched opportunistically (e.g. next time an FMP-backed edge function is deployed under an unrelated charter). No SLA.

**(3) MONEY-PATH VERIFICATION — FMP field-name bug scope confirmed BOUNDED (does not touch exclusion path).**

The live detector's earnings-proximity exclusion reads `overshoot_earnings_calendar.announcement_date` (the ISO date), which is populated by the FMP fetcher from FMP response field `date` — NOT one of the four bug-affected fields. The bug affected only surprise/estimate numerics: `epsActual`, `revenueActual`, `epsEstimated`, `revenueEstimated` (see `supabase/functions/_shared/overshoot/earnings-calendar-fetcher.ts` inline comment marking the four repaired names verbatim). Announcement-date parsing has always been correct.

**Cited fields (verbatim from `earnings-calendar-fetcher.ts`, FmpEarningsRow):**
- `date` → `announcement_date` (**unaffected — exclusion path reads this**)
- `symbol` → `ticker` (unaffected)
- `epsActual` / `revenueActual` / `epsEstimated` / `revenueEstimated` (the four bug-affected numeric fields — surprise-computation only)

**Proof query (executed 2026-07-14):**
```sql
SELECT source, COUNT(*) AS total, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE announcement_date IS NULL) AS null_dates,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE announcement_date::text ~ '^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$') AS parses_iso
FROM overshoot_earnings_calendar GROUP BY source;
```
Result:

| source | total | null_dates | parses_iso |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| finnhub |  16,572 | 0 |  16,572 |
| fmp     | 356,468 | 0 | 356,468 |
| **all** | **373,040** | **0** | **373,040** |

**Verdict:** 373,040 / 373,040 exclusion-date rows parse as ISO dates with zero nulls. The FMP field-name bug is confined to surprise/estimate numerics. The detector's exclusion window logic has never admitted an event inside an earnings window because of this bug. **NO INC filed** — bug scope is bounded to a research-only path (surprise-magnitude computation for PEAD study), and PEAD is shelved.

**(4) Strategy-#3 question — CLOSED.**
No new-strategy candidate currently clears the OVERSHOOT dominance floor (42.42 bps/slot-day). Both feasibility studies chartered this cycle failed:
- **ACT-520 put-write proxy:** 18.08 bps/slot-day (42.6 % of floor) → SHELF-UNLESS-REAL-IV (needs ≥2.4× premium uplift vs proxy, unsupported by equity-options literature). Tradier forward-observation plan filed dormant.
- **ACT-521 PEAD:** 36.13 bps/slot-day best cell (85 % of floor) after honesty gates → SHELVE structural (this filing).

**Marginal-capital ruling:** the best measured use of the next dollar of capital remains **additional OVERSHOOT slots**. The live growth levers — all already ratified, no new-strategy dependency — are:
1. **ACT-510** — tier-conditional entry-day + exit-horizon (T1 timing tune, landing this week).
2. **DEC-504-4** — sleeve reallocation (recycling capital across T1/T2/T3 per ratified caps).
3. **ACT-511** — U2 universe expansion (the supply-side path to more T1 slots).

**Strategy scouting resumes at Phase-L scale** — the AUM point where OVERSHOOT's event supply saturates (ACT-511 measures this threshold; per the Operator Dominance Test standing rule, diversification value only counts at that scale). Until then, strategy-#3 is a NON-QUESTION: capital deploys into OVERSHOOT, period.

## ACT-528 (2026-07-15) — INC-106 DIRECTION FIX + ACT-527 EXECUTION + STRATEGY-SCAFFOLD RULING (three-part dispatch)

### Part 2 — ACT-527 (a)–(d) APPROVED, executing

**Deliverable widened at zero marginal cost** (single SI backfill funds all three axes):

1. **(a) Short P&L** — SI-bucket × regime × horizon {3,5,10}d. Threshold re-derivation evidence for the exclusion gate.
2. **(b) Long-flip SQUEEZE-RIDE CANDIDATE** — same grid, opposite side. Tests whether high-SI names are LONGABLE (ride the squeeze) rather than merely shortable.
3. **(c) Trailing-stop ladder grid** for the flip, simulated on daily OHLC (granularity caveat stated: intraday trigger noise unmeasured — bull-case ceiling, not fidelity claim). Ladders: `{initial 20/15/10%} × {tighten step 2.5/5% per +5% gain} × {floor 5/7.5%}` + no-stop baseline; per-slot-day economics net of stop-outs per cell.

**Pre-committed adoption rules (FROZEN, cited before any number exists):**
- Dominance floor vs OVERSHOOT slots at **15%-class margin** (i.e. ≥ 15% above the OVERSHOOT 42.42 bps/slot-day floor per bucket claimed for adoption).
- **n ≥ 1000** per adopted cell.
- **Monotone-stable** across adjacent SI buckets and regime strata (no cherry-picked isolated cell).
- **Regime stratum DISPOSITIVE:** bull-only edge yields at most a REGIME-GATED sleeve proposal with 2022 bear-cost quantified — never an all-weather adoption.
- **Capacity priced:** events/yr per qualifying bucket, so any adoption comes with a realistic slot-count.

**Execution sequence (this filing = start-of-run):**
1. Feasibility probe (1 Polygon call — pin field shape + date coverage).
2. Dry-run (1 batch — pin idempotent upsert into `overshoot_short_interest`).
3. 14-invocation production backfill (~839 calls across 14 edge-function batches).
4. Coverage verification (target ≥ 95% of the 4-year corpus with a non-null SI row).
5. Regime-stratified curve (all three axes above), pre-committed rule evaluation.

### Part 3 — STRATEGY-SCAFFOLD RULING (structure ratified; BUILD GATED on curve verdict)

**Ruling filed to charter (this action = the charter entry):**

If ACT-527(b) — the long-flip squeeze-ride candidate — clears the pre-committed rules above, it charters as:
- A **NEW strategy module** (not an addition to OVERSHOOT). `src/features/<squeezeride>/`, own docs at `docs/04-modules/<squeezeride>/`, own perms `<squeezeride>.{view,manage,execute}`, own tables `<squeezeride>_*`, own edge functions `<squeezeride>-*`, own audit table `<squeezeride>_audit_logs` — full T1–T9 discipline.
- A **NEW Alpaca paper account #3** (secrets `ALPACA_PAPER_KEY_SQUEEZERIDE` / `ALPACA_PAPER_SECRET_SQUEEZERIDE`; the paper-only URL fence and PA-account-number allowlist extend one row). Same one-brain-many-wallets shape as the ACT-459 overshoot-broker split from longshort-broker.
- Its **own trading-panel console section** at `/trading/<squeezeride>/`, registered via `src/config/trading-navigation.ts` (T5 façade-import carve-out).

**Rationale for the structural separation** (opposite-side rule): OVERSHOOT and squeeze-ride would take **opposite sides of the same underlying events** — a high-SI event that OVERSHOOT (post-fix) refuses as `si_above_squeeze_threshold` is exactly the event squeeze-ride would enter LONG. Sharing a book would produce internal offset, contaminated attribution, and cross-strategy lot-selection risk. They must live as independent books with independent capital.

**Build gate:** ZERO build turns until the ACT-527 curve rules. No premature scaffolding, no "prep work" — the curve verdict is the sole trigger. If the flip fails the pre-committed rules, this ruling files as a NULL charter and the scaffold is never built.

**Cross-references:** `_shared/overshoot/detector/detector.ts` (INC-106 fix, direction + version bump); `detector_test.ts` (R2 canaries); `docs/08-planning/approved-decisions.md:852` (R2 ratification); ACT-526 (pre-committed curve rule); ACT-527 (SI backfill charter, now executing); ACT-459 (one-brain-many-wallets precedent — overshoot-broker split from longshort-broker); INC-106 (direction-inversion defect, now closed by this fix).

## ACT-529 — Cross-function version-propagation audit (RATIFIED_DETECTOR_VERSION a026dc51)

**Trigger:** Operator directive after INC-106 direction fix bumped `RATIFIED_DETECTOR_VERSION` from `b7cdfcd8` → `a026dc51`. Only `overshoot-detection-run` was redeployed in that turn; entry-run, exit-run, and fill-sweep continued to serve pre-fix bundles carrying the old constant. Half-propagated version constants across a linked pipeline is a defect class regardless of whether today's code path compares them.

**(a) Cross-function detector_version comparison — source-audited (READ-ONLY).**
- `overshoot-entry-run/index.ts` fetches the linked detection run via `SELECT run_id::text AS run_id, as_of::text AS as_of, outcome, selected_count FROM overshoot_detection_runs` (line 535–537) and joins `overshoot_events e JOIN overshoot_detection_runs dr ON dr.run_id = e.run_id` (line 679–680) selecting `e.ticker, e.side, e.rank_score, e.tier, e.argmax_window_days, dr.as_of` — **no column reads `dr.detector_version` and no comparison exists between the fetched row's stamp and the bundled `RATIFIED_DETECTOR_VERSION` constant.** The constant is only echoed OUTBOUND into audit metadata (lines 388, 407, 718, 1212), never compared inbound.
- `overshoot-exit-run/index.ts` — line :307 is the cron-first auth branch (`X-Cron-Secret` verification per INC-99/ACT-503), not a detector_version canary. The file's only detector_version usage is (i) the boot-format assert at line 381–388 against the bundled constant and (ii) probe-envelope echo (lines 404, 424). Exit-run reads `overshoot_lots` and open positions; it never joins `overshoot_detection_runs` or reads any `detector_version` column.
- `overshoot-fill-sweep/index.ts` — same pattern: boot-format assert (line 189) + outbound echo (lines 205, 224, 824). No inbound comparison.

**Answer to (a):** NO — none of entry-run, exit-run, or fill-sweep validates a linked detection run's `detector_version` against its bundled `RATIFIED_DETECTOR_VERSION`. Tomorrow's slot-a would NOT have refused the `a026dc51` book on version-linkage grounds even if entry-run had continued serving the `b7cdfcd8` bundle. The pipeline's version discipline today is boot-format-only (per-function, in isolation).

**(b) Class rule filed (per operator directive):**
> **CLASS RULE (ratified 2026-07-15):** A `RATIFIED_DETECTOR_VERSION` bump requires redeploying EVERY edge function that imports the constant, in the SAME landing. Functions with the import today: `overshoot-detection-run`, `overshoot-entry-run`, `overshoot-exit-run`, `overshoot-fill-sweep`. Half-propagated version constants across a linked pipeline is a defect class independent of whether the code path currently compares them — the invariant is "one constant value across the pipeline at any deployed instant." A CI/pre-commit guard is deferred to ACT-530 (below); until then, any turn that edits `RATIFIED_DETECTOR_VERSION` MUST redeploy all four functions in the same turn and confirm via OPTIONS probe.

**Action taken this turn:** Redeployed `overshoot-entry-run`, `overshoot-exit-run`, `overshoot-fill-sweep` (Wed 2026-07-15 ~11:24Z). Detection-run was already deployed with `a026dc51` in the INC-106 fix turn. All four functions now bundle `a026dc51`.

**(c) Tonight's 22:00Z detection expectation (unchanged from the INC-106 ruling):**

- Post-21:00Z SI-heal → high-SI residuals (HIMS, etc.) reach the squeeze gate; under the flipped exclusion semantics they refuse with reason `si_above_squeeze_threshold` (R2-safe state). Report to be filed after the 22:00Z run.

**(d) Tomorrow's 13:35Z slot-a expectation:**

## ACT-531 — Signal-conditioned continuation map (INVESTIGATION, queued behind ACT-527)

**Mode:** INVESTIGATION — read-only corpus compute. Same executor lane as ACT-527; kicks off when ACT-527's backfill + curve compute completes (no contention, strict sequencing). No live-gate change may reference this work until the deliverable lands and the operator rules.

**Operator hypothesis under test:** upward dislocations that carry an identifiable catalyst signature should CONTINUE (trend), in contrast to OVERSHOOT's premise that no-signal dislocations REVERT. The deliverable is the direction map — per-bucket "continue / revert / flat" with the measured number — not a strategy.

### Method (pre-committed before any number exists)

1. **Event set.** Scan the full `overshoot_daily_bars` corpus for UPWARD dislocations using the OVERSHOOT excess geometry mirrored to the upside — same |excess| thresholds, same momentum/drawdown bands — but **without** the earnings exclusion. This is a NEW event set (not the overshoot corpus); it must be materialised as its own study cell surface.
2. **Buckets (catalyst signature within ±3 trading days of the event, in-db sources only):**
   - (a) **earnings-proximate** — `overshoot_earnings_calendar` (~373k rows)
   - (b) **analyst-action-proximate** — grades / price-target changes (longshort FMP tables)
   - (c) **M&A / news-proximate** — longshort catalyst tables (`classify-catalyst-event` output)
   - (d) **insider-proximate** — Form 4 activity (`insider_form4_rows`)
   - (e) **high-SI** — `si_pct_float >= 0.15` on the ACT-527 backfilled SI corpus (the squeeze signature; cite ACT-527 rather than recompute)
   - (f) **no-identifiable-signal** — none of (a)–(e); the pure-noise bucket
3. **Cuts.** Report both EXCLUSIVE (each event assigned to at most one primary bucket by precedence) and OVERLAPPING (an event may appear in multiple buckets) surfaces. Overlap matrix is part of the deliverable.
4. **Return grid.** For each bucket × regime × horizon ∈ {3, 5, 10, 21} trading days: forward return LONG and SHORT from **T+1 open buyable basis**, per-slot-day economics, n, events/yr. Regime strata as per ACT-527 (bull/bear/chop tags on SPY).

### Deliverable: the direction map

One table per bucket answering **continue (go long) / revert (go short) / flat (no trade)** with the measured statistic (bps/slot-day, n, events/yr), plus the honest overlays:

- **(i) Cross-check.** Bucket (f) — no-signal — SHORT side must reproduce the ACT-527 short curve within noise. Divergence here is a methods finding that invalidates the whole surface, not a discovery.
- **(ii) Squeeze-ride carve-out.** Bucket (e) IS the squeeze-ride surface studied under ACT-527/528; **cite** the ACT-527 numbers rather than recompute. Any duplicated compute must match — divergence is a methods finding.
- **(iii) PEAD reconciliation.** Bucket (a) LONG side must reconcile with the PEAD full-panel rerun (~14 bps/day baseline). Divergence is a methods finding.
- **(iv) Arbitrage-density disclosure.** Catalyst-continuation is a heavily-arbitraged space. The dominance floor is **frozen NOW**, before any number is seen, and decides adoption:
  - `>= 42.42 bps/slot-day` vs the frozen OVERSHOOT deployment baseline
  - 15%-class margin
  - `n >= 1000`
  - monotone across the bucket ordering being claimed
  - regime-stratum dispositive (per-regime, not pooled)

### Stop rule

**STOP after the map for operator review.** ACT-531 charters no strategy, edits no gate, and adds no code path outside the study surface. Any strategy that follows charters SEPARATELY under the ACT-528 scaffold rules (own module, own Alpaca account, own console section — the one-brain-many-wallets shape), and only after operator ratification of a specific bucket-direction claim against the frozen dominance floor.

### Sequencing

- **T0:** ACT-527 backfill + curve compute completes.
- **T0 + step 1:** materialise the upward-dislocation event set (mirrored excess geometry, no earnings exclusion) into `overshoot_study_candidate_events` under a new `study_cell` tag; verify count is plausible before proceeding.
- **T0 + step 2:** join catalyst-signature buckets (a)–(e) from in-db sources; produce exclusive + overlapping partition telemetry.
- **T0 + step 3:** compute per-bucket × regime × horizon return grid from T+1-open basis; write to `overshoot_study_cell_results` under the ACT-531 run tag.
- **T0 + step 4:** produce the direction-map table + the four overlays (i)–(iv); operator review; **STOP**.
